purpose: Reconcile all six deliberately unsigned application rows from v332 with existing exam questions and five new manually assessed application problems.

rows.subject: Physics
rows.skill: Combine physical estimates in a derived order-of-magnitude application
rows.notes: The new climb example combines geometry, energy, power and a power-of-ten judgement. Numerical reasoning requires actual written working.
rows.applicationAvailability: sample practice available; manual work required

rows.subject: Chemistry
rows.skill: Write and use the direct Arrhenius equation as well as its logarithmic form
rows.notes: The existing graph question uses the log form; the new question requires direct k=A exp(−Ea/RT) substitution and comparison across temperatures.
rows.applicationAvailability: sample practice available; manual work required

rows.subject: Chemistry
rows.skill: Calculate unfamiliar numerical rate constants from Arrhenius parameters
rows.notes: A new direct numerical calculation complements the existing independently specified Arrhenius graph problem.
rows.applicationAvailability: sample practice available; manual work required

rows.subject: Chemistry
rows.skill: Use initial rates and continuous monitoring and understand methodological limits
rows.notes: Existing quantitative initial-rate and concentration-time tasks are supplemented by a practical-design comparison with a clock endpoint.
rows.applicationAvailability: sample practice available; manual work required

rows.subject: Chemistry
rows.skill: Carry out whole-process Kp calculations from equilibrium composition and partial pressures
rows.notes: Existing mole-to-Kp calculation now has a complementary inverse Kp-to-composition problem.
rows.applicationAvailability: sample practice available; manual work required

rows.subject: Chemistry
rows.skill: Explain why a catalyst can speed equilibrium attainment but leaves Kp unchanged
rows.notes: New separate explanation explicitly tests catalyst effect on both reaction directions, equilibrium composition and Kp at constant temperature.
rows.applicationAvailability: sample practice available; manual work required

limitations: Practice question presence is not proof of a student's competence.
The detailed AQA all-subsections audit and real-world handwritten-answer review still remain.
The website deliberately withholds automatic marks for multi-stage science answers until manually reviewed.
